title: Ninth Word Fifth Point Bowing And Prostration With The Universe General Result

questions.question: What does the person say while bending down in prayer?
questions.answer: He says that Allah is the Greatest.

questions.question: What are the sleeping plants, animals, stars, and suns compared to?
questions.answer: They are like soldiers, lamps, and servants under Allah’s command.

questions.question: What big idea does the person think about before bowing?
questions.answer: He thinks about Allah’s greatness and power.

questions.question: What happens to many creatures over time, like each year or century?
questions.answer: They finish their jobs and pass away in an orderly way.

questions.question: In the passage, what does the death of creatures resemble?
questions.answer: It is like a great prostration.

questions.question: What helps creatures come to life again, especially in spring?
questions.answer: Allah’s command brings them back to life.

questions.question: What does the person do after thinking about creatures that bow and rise again?
questions.answer: He also says that Allah is the Greatest and makes prostration.

questions.question: How does the person feel when he prostrates?
questions.answer: He feels loving wonder, humility, and lowliness before Allah.

questions.question: What is prostration called in a special way here?
questions.answer: It is described as a kind of rising upward to Allah.

questions.question: Why does the passage say the night prayer is good and fitting?
questions.answer: Because it is a meaningful act of worship at an important time.

questions.question: What does each of the five prayer times point to?
questions.answer: Each one points to a great change and Allah’s mighty actions.

questions.question: Why are the required prayers set at certain times?
questions.answer: Because that is wise, and those times match Allah’s blessings and signs.

questions.question: When the worshipper says that Allah is the Greatest, what does he do next?
questions.answer: He bends in prayer.

questions.question: Which parts of creation are said to be resting at that time?
questions.answer: The plants and animals are resting.

questions.question: How are the stars described in the passage?
questions.answer: They are shown as serious and obedient.

questions.question: Who is in control of all these created things?
questions.answer: Allah is in control of them.

questions.question: What command of Allah is mentioned to show His power?
questions.answer: His command that something comes into being when He wills it.

questions.question: What happens to creatures when their time of duty ends?
questions.answer: They are sent away from this world in an orderly way.

questions.question: What season is given as an example of things coming back to life?
questions.answer: Spring.

questions.question: How is man connected to the other creatures in this part?
questions.answer: He follows their example by praising Allah and prostrating.

questions.question: In whose presence does man prostrate?
questions.answer: In the presence of Allah, the Most Merciful and Most Compassionate.

questions.question: What two feelings are joined with the person’s prostration?
questions.answer: Love and humility.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the value of the night prayer?
questions.answer: It says it is beautiful, joyful, proper, and important.

questions.question: What is one reason the five daily prayers are placed at special times?
questions.answer: Those times show great changes and Allah’s gifts.

questions.question: What does the worshipper remember about Allah before bowing down?
questions.answer: He remembers Allah’s majesty.

questions.question: How does the passage show that creation obeys Allah?
questions.answer: It says creation is like an army that follows orders.

questions.question: What are the heavenly lights in the world compared to?
questions.answer: They are compared to lamps.

questions.question: What happens to the earth and the universe in the example of prostration?
questions.answer: They too are pictured as obeying Allah and lowering themselves like servants.

questions.question: Is the passing away of creatures shown as messy or ordered?
questions.answer: It is shown as ordered.

questions.question: What happens after some creatures die and later return in spring?
questions.answer: They rise again and get ready to serve Allah.

questions.question: What does man say when following this pattern of creation?
questions.answer: He says that Allah is the Greatest.

questions.question: What kind of heart does man have while prostrating?
questions.answer: He has a heart full of wonder, love, and humbleness.

questions.question: What does the passage suggest prostration can help a person do?
questions.answer: It can lift him spiritually toward Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the night prayer as an act of worship?
questions.answer: It describes it as lovely, uplifting, and sensible.

questions.question: What do the five prayer times show us besides big changes?
questions.answer: They also show Allah’s blessings.

questions.question: According to the passage, why is praying at these times the right thing to do?
questions.answer: Because the prayers are a duty, and those times are chosen with wisdom.

questions.question: What words does the worshipper say as he thinks about Allah’s greatness?
questions.answer: He says that Allah is the Greatest.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about animals and plants at night?
questions.answer: They are resting under Allah’s rule.

questions.question: What lesson do the stars and suns give in this part?
questions.answer: They show that even huge things obey Allah.

questions.question: What picture is used for all creatures together?
questions.answer: They are pictured like a well-ordered army.

questions.question: When creatures leave this world, what action are they compared to?
questions.answer: They are compared to making prostration.

questions.question: What shows Allah can bring life again after death?
questions.answer: The return of life in spring shows that.

questions.question: How should a human being respond after thinking about these signs?
questions.answer: He should praise Allah and prostrate.

questions.question: What good manners of the heart are named for the one who prostrates?
questions.answer: Loving awe, humility, and lowering oneself before Allah.

questions.question: What special name is given to this act of worship at the end of prostration?
questions.answer: It is called a kind of ascent.

questions.question: Does the passage present the night prayer as a small matter or an important one?
questions.answer: It presents it as very important.

questions.question: What does each prayer time point toward in Allah’s creation?
questions.answer: It points toward a great turning or change.

questions.question: Why is it wise for prayers to be fixed at these times?
questions.answer: Because these times are signs of Allah’s actions and gifts.

questions.question: During the night prayer, what does the person think about first before bowing?
questions.answer: He thinks about Allah’s greatness.

questions.question: In this passage, what are created things like because they follow Allah’s command?
questions.answer: They are like obedient workers and soldiers.

questions.question: What do lamps in the world picture help us understand?
questions.answer: They help us understand that creation serves under Allah’s rule.

questions.question: What happens again and again to many living things over the years?
questions.answer: They complete their time and pass away.

questions.question: How does the passage describe their going away?
questions.answer: It describes it as orderly and obedient.

questions.question: What season gives hope by showing life returning?
questions.answer: Spring gives that hope.

questions.question: What does man do after seeing that creatures die and live again by Allah’s will?
questions.answer: He follows by saying that Allah is the Greatest and by prostrating.

questions.question: What makes his prostration more than just body movement?
questions.answer: He is filled with wonder, love, and humble respect.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying this is a kind of ascension?
questions.answer: It means the worshipper is spiritually raised toward Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage help us feel about the 'Isha prayer?
questions.answer: It helps us see it as beautiful, pleasant, and meaningful.

questions.question: What two things do the five prayer times stand for in the passage?
questions.answer: Great changes and divine gifts.

questions.question: Why are these prayer times not random?
questions.answer: Because they are chosen with wisdom and fit their special meanings.

questions.question: What does the worshipper say when thinking about Allah’s strong power over all things?
questions.answer: He says that Allah is the Greatest.

questions.question: Name two kinds of created things in the passage that are under Allah’s command.
questions.answer: Plants and animals.

questions.question: What do the hidden suns and calm stars show about Allah?
questions.answer: They show His greatness and control.

questions.question: What example is given to show that all creatures obey together?
questions.answer: They are described like a disciplined army.

questions.question: What is one way the passage describes death?
questions.answer: It describes death like a prostration of creation.

questions.question: After creatures are brought back, what are they ready to do?
questions.answer: They are ready to serve their Lord.

questions.question: What should a person learn from the way creation bows and rises?
questions.answer: He should worship Allah with praise and prostration.

questions.question: What feelings should fill the heart in prostration according to the passage?
questions.answer: Wonder, love, humility, and self-lowliness.

questions.question: What is the result of this worship, in a special spiritual sense?
questions.answer: It becomes a kind of upward nearness to Allah.

questions.question: How does the passage describe the duty of the 'Isha prayer?
questions.answer: It describes it as noble, joyful, fitting, and serious.

questions.question: What does every one of the five prayer times signal?
questions.answer: It signals a great change and Allah’s active care.

questions.question: Why should the required prayers be done at these times?
questions.answer: Because these times are full of meaning, blessings, and wisdom.
